overall_summary: Analysis of recent YouTube Shorts performance for FACTVERSE reveals a clear audience preference for high-concept space and planetary 'what-if' or extreme environmental scenarios published within the last 7 days. Specifically, speculative cosmic scenarios and extreme planetary attributes (e.g., Venus day length, liquid diamond planets, burning ice planets) achieve the highest views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes-per-view). Conversely, older psychological tricks and standard biological facts exhibit significantly lower velocity and engagement, indicating saturation or weaker initial hook potency.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0, 980 views), 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y, 1024 views), and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68, 972 views) show exceptionally high view counts and strong like ratios relative to older content.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on speculative astronomical scenarios and bizarre planetary physics using high-stakes hypothetical phrasing ('What if you fell into...').

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre Reality Checks on Time and Scale
winning_patterns.evidence: Recent space/physics hooks addressing mind-bending scales like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) generated over 700 to 1000+ views rapidly.
winning_patterns.action: Maintain short durations (15-21 seconds) with immediate visual contrast and shocking superlatives in the opening seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: Content focused on songs stuck in your head or minor memory facts ('The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head', 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') stalled under 100 views with minimal likes over prolonged periods.
weak_patterns.action: De-prioritize mundane human psychology tips unless framed as extreme medical anomalies or high-stakes neurological mysteries.

weak_patterns.evidence: Recycled animal facts like octopuses having three hearts show diminishing returns on repeat iterations compared to planetary anomalies.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal and nature content away from standard trivia toward cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary adaptations.
